IF your goal is to complete the game and call it a day, I get why it's not very liked, but if you actually want to ghost a level, oh boy you're in for a challenge!

“Thief” is so disappointing on so many levels.

Pros: Excellent visual aesthetic. Scenery looks phenomenal and the sense of dampness, filth, lighting, and props lend a lot toward immersion. Weaponry, though limited, is interesting. Sneaking around is quite fun.

Cons: Linear, closed world. Narrow, almost claustrophobic corridor for exploration. Climbing tools are made available and fun to use but you may only climb in certain areas related to the path you are forced to take in the game. No clambering up on random boxes, roofs or pipes even if they look identical to the ones you are allowed to climb on. The world is very static, with a limited amount of interaction. Most doors cannot be opened. There is one story and you have to follow it or quit the game. I knew the game wouldn't be as open as Skyrim but was expecting at least the level of freedom that was available in a game like Dishonored, or maybe even Assassin's Creed. The game is gorgeous to look at, but it feels pointless. Not what I expect a game to be like in this decade.

The game is called Thief, you play a thief... but stealing loot is merely incidental, whereas listening to conversations and looking through knotholes for clues that lead you through the story is far more important. At most the player is just a kleptomaniac. The game should be called “Voyeur”. The only sense of real accomplishment to be found is in not being seen – being a “Ghost”. There is no enjoyment in collecting riches because there is very little to purchase with your coin. As for loot, it's repetitive and placed is utterly illogical places. The city is in squalor, yet you can find a sterling brush just sitting on a crate next to a vagrant or a golden cup on a secluded rooftop. There are special items to be found but in the end it's all about how sneaky you are, not how much you were able to steal.

Finally, a word on violence. I like both non-violent and violent games, though I prefer the latter. This game provides many opportunities for violence and the overall violent atmosphere of the game actually provokes the player to act on it, yet he player is penalized for using violence, and ultimately for even being seen. It's like putting candy on the table and telling a kid not to eat it. 

Summary: This game had enormous potential but pissed it away. You pay $50 to be teased and ultimately let down. Use your $50 to go on a date.

It's an okay taffer game. The story was okay, but it was way too short, and it could have been told better. Gameplay is good, but holy mackerel, animations for opening the windows or crossing the gaps were really annoying. If the game is on sale, you can try and [strike]steal it[/strike] buy it.

First you'll cringe at Garrett's new voice. Then you'll wince at the new story. Then you blink, absorbing the visuals and trying to ignore the audio. Then you warm up to the game, starting to appreciate the reboot's new direction. Then you start to enjoy yourself, getting into the meat of the level designs and AI quirks. And then you facepalm, repeatedly, non-stop, forever, as the story erodes every last shred of goodwill, with cheese-bursting cutscenes about ghostly energy and Primals and megalomaniacal siblings unleashing cult members to change the world. 

They could have scrapped the hub town, deleted the story, and just made ~10 large intricate sneaking levels, saving production money, and everything would have been fine, even without Garrett's old voice. 

As a game, Thief is competent, even beautiful, and its apparent many people worked hard on it. Buy it on sale and get lost for a few weekends. 

As a Thief branded game, its a disappointing mess, discarding old characters and methods for misguided AAA marketing ideas and can only be recommended for rubbernecking at the train wreck. 

No Hammerites, no Pagans, no taffers. But plenty of expletive-laden spit-shined shlock.

"Thi4f" might have excellent level design, gripping story and incredible characters. I still wouldn't care, it's so overanimated playing it feels like pulling teeth. 

What do I mean by that? You don't really "control" Garret in this one. you just interact with endless short pre-animated sequences. Opening a door? Press E and watch for 3 seconds of your character grabbing the handle, pushing the door and going back to his starting position. Looting a desk? Watch EIGHT 1-2 second long animations of opening and closing drawers. Frigging' JUMPING DOWN THE LEDGE? Another cutscene. They can't even let gravity do it's own thing, you will jump down JUZT AS ZE GAME INTENDED or you won't do it at all. I hate it so, SO much. There is a reason so many things are abstracted in games (like picking up loot instantly) - because doing them "the realistic way" is boring and stupid. But once in a while someone thinks they know better, and creates a game that "fixes" those inconsistencies. Those games suck. This is one of such games.

So, I've sunk another 9 hours into this game and my opinion hasn't changed. This basically is a worse dishonored. Ironically, it's mindblowingly similar to it, but with a lot less commitment to almost every aspect of it. You want to play ultra stealth? Learn the paths of every npc and just follow in their shadow, or just walk past right in front of them. As long as you're coated in shadows, they won't see you. If there's a lightsource, worry not. You can shoot out every fire and turn off every light. But not really, since there are quite a lot of lamps, which you cannot turn off, or destroy in any way. Do you want to go after every guard? You'll execute them with one button prompt, but you might as well just 1v1 them in an honorable battle, in which they only know attack and defense. The Ai in general likes to bug out, after reloading savegames. But I've bought this game for one reason and one reason only: Steal stuff. And even though, this is well implemented, the story really doesn't give you any reason to play. The ending especially confuses me every time, I see it. They'll try and, in a roundabout way, connect the intro struggle with the end and it doesn't work. You'll know what the writers tried to do, but you'll realise, that they just destroy every character developement Garret went through in your 9 hour journey. Luckily though, you don't need to replay the story, to replay chapters. The climbing is half-bad implemented, the soundtrack is unremarkable, the soundeffects are passable and the artstyle is great. The voice-acting doesn't sound right in certain scenes and the performance is passable.

people hate this game for no reason. it plays fine and looks good. people hate it because its not exactly like Thief 1 and 2. the game might not live up to those standards but by itself its a very good game and people who dont think so just cant look past their own nostalgia

 ✅ You can continue playing after beating the game

The Bad

❌ You will be opening a lot of empty drawers and cupboards.

[u] Gameplay [/u]
Thief is a stealth video game, It is a revival of the cult classic Thief video game series of which it is the fourth installment. Initially announced in 2009 as Thief 4, it was later announced in 2013 that the game is a reboot for the series.

The game is set in 'The City', a dark fantasy world inspired by Victorian, Gothic, and steampunk aesthetics. Players control Garrett, a master thief who embarks on several missions focusing on stealing from the rich. Players may approach levels in a variety of different ways; players can choose the action oriented and lethal approach, where players will disable or kill enemies on their way to their destination, using knives and takedowns, or opt for the non-lethal stealthy approach, where players minimize interaction with NPCs and the environment in order to avoid detection. Players also may choose which path to take to their destination, as each location contains several branching paths.

I cannot give it a negative review for what it is, since overall it's a proper game. As long as you condition yourself to clear levels only by stealth – and I assume that's the way it's meant to be played – the experience is complete. You study the enemy, plan the route, wait for your moment, use the environment, move silently, and grab everything you can along the way.

And while it works in the beginning, where the challenge is still fearly managable for a smooth and clean playthrough, in the later levels… the complexity needed for achieving this kind of a run becomes just too much. The locations get bigger and bigger, the enemies are plentiful, the alarm triggers get scattered all over your path, and you end up being just simply… painfully slowed down and wary of literally EVERYTHING. Is it worthy of a master thief? Yes. Is it fun as a video game meant for fun and relaxation? No.

And, as I'm assuming many players did, you end up just killing or stunning everyone, since it's easier and faster. And boring. But not much less boring than sitting in dark corners for minutes studying enemy patrols and their lines of sight, looking for noisy crows, sniffing dogs, scattered glass, traps, holes, places for takedowns, etc.

The game also has this action adventure dark fantasy background which… kind of… takes over. Somewhere along the way you lose the feeling of being simply a thief, and instead you become this dark knight who tries to save the city from monsters. It seems actually weird, picking up coins and jewellery from behind the backs of horror mutant creatures while the city is dying and turning into a nightmare… Makes you think: "What is wrong with you, Garret?"

So, yeah… it's all good, as long as you want a "chore" of a stealth game (with, eh… monsters), but if you just want to move smoothly in the shadows of the night, speed through rooftops, rob some folks while they're busy reading, occasionally move past some guards – you WILL GET that through the first half of the game, and then… it's "go get them, tiger".

This game is plagued by strange design decisions and technical issues. Overall it is a bad successor to the previous installments in the series.
Pros:
- graphics were awesome back in 2014 and do not look very dated now.
- first-person animations are neat.
Cons:
- bugs and technical issues. Had lots of issues with NPC AI. Sometimes they are stuck after being alerted and do not return to their patrol paths. After reloading AI sometimes breaks: NPCs start going somewhere they aren't supposed to or just stand still. Usually, they stop being alerted after some seconds but sometimes they just do not stop being alerted. There are times when game prevents saving for no reason (enemies are not alerted, after reloading works fine). Game loading is incomplete as game drops framerate 5-10 sec after loading screen is gone obviously still loading something.
- sound design. In this game sound was pretty much useless as it almost never hinted me direction of enemies which is essential in stealth game.
- context-based actions. Most things you can do in this game are context-based, meaning you can shoot rope arrow only in specific places, you can climb objects only in specific places and so on. Such design shines in latest Hitman games due to amount, diversity and creativity of interactions. In thief levels are mostly linear, there is no diversity to interactions, and it all leads to boring level exploration unlike in previous games in the series. Controls are clunky as the same button is used for multiple interactions: you can drop from crate instead of jumping to rope leading to being found and reloading. Also jumping is inconsistent: in some places game prevents jumping to death and it can feel that you can jump only in safe places, but in other places game will allow you to jump to your death while you expect character to jump safely.
- plot. It is awful. Bad writing, bad cutscenes. Focus on Erin character who is unlikeable and whom we as players know for nearly 10 minutes. Thief-taker character is not involved into plot in any meaningful way. It seems writers just needed some antagonist who is "killing-subordinates-cliche-kind-of-evil". The Graven take over the city behind the scenes when we know almost nothing about them. Ending is... strange and probably rushed. Garret activates book for no reason instead of simply giving claw to Erin. And shift between last gameplay scene and last cutscene feels unfinished.
- 3rd person parkour is joke. It could be used to allow multiple paths on locations, but it is mostly used in linear sequences where there are no other ways. And it ruins immersion as it is the only time you see protagonist from 3rd person during gameplay. 
- trophies are junk. There are less than 5 interesting trophies in this game, most trophies are some rings lying in piles of junk, where it can be hard to spot them even if you know where they should be. Only few trophies are somehow hinted beforehand and connected to the story or locations. 
- lots of "loading" gates, where you press E or smth to move forward. They are always the same: both animation and visuals. Obviously, they also break immersion. Similar issues were present in Deadly shadows, but it seems to me that even there levels were larger.
- boring protagonist. There are very few interesting lines from him in entire game and humor/cynicism from previous games in series is almost completely gone.
- boring setting. Plagued city is extremely basic idea, but this game does not have much more to offer. Lore of previous games was much more interesting, and it is strange they decided to reboot setting without looking back.
- bad level design. There are few non-linear levels and even they are not particularly good and do not have much freedom. For me, the best level was Northcrest mansion, but it is pretty basic compared to other thief games or more morern Dishonored ones. Moira asylum could be great due to horror element, but it was ruined for me by lots of "press-E-to-procceed" doors and lots of boring and mostly empty cells which are not that fun to explore.
- bad notes. Only place with interesting and insightful notes was Northcrest mansion while on other locations most notes are garbage not adding much to story or lore. Also notes are strangely implemented. When you activate them once they are added to your journal and you can read them there. You cannot activate notes once more inside game world and journal does not track order or location where note was taken. Sometimes it can lead to being stuck with some puzzle as you don't know which notes were found nearby as only they matter.

Pros:

- Graphics.
- Diverse locations (my favorite one: horror-like Moira Asylum).
- Open-world city to chill out in between missions.
- It's easy to track and follow quests.

Cons:

- Blocking animations for every single thing you do. Quite irritating to see (and wait for) them every time you need to open or loot sth (which is - suprise - really often).
- Sometimes clumsy controls for movement.
- Poor, not immersive story telling.
- Solving problems seems more like finding the path put there by developers rather then tackling them your own way (because most of the time there are no options). Some places (important for current mission) are simply inaccessible from another path - even if it should not be a problem to jump there (and by that I mean - it should not be a problem even for normal people).

Overall:

It's playable, I have finished it (and at the end enjoyed it) and would recommend to buy when it's on sale. The main con is just the fact the standard for stealth games was set quite high by Dishonored - the new Thief tries [sometimes too] hard to be like it but comes short.

I am a die hard Thief fan stretching back to the beginning of Thief time. Yep, I'm old...50 to be precise. I've been playing video games since Intellivision was a thing and Mt. St. Helens was a recent event. I like this game, but there are two things that make it less appealing to me than previous Thief games: Unnecessary X-rated content (very small scene but still, why do that?) and a flat, uninteresting story line. The game play is ridiculously addictive. And this Thief can fight! The fighting UX is far better than any of the previous games, without going too far and turning this into some flavor of Assassin's Creed. I really don't care what mission I'm on in these types of games, so the flat storyline is a minor annoyance. With immersive sims the joy is in the gameplay, not so much finishing a story like in an Adventure game. So, I really don't care much about a flat story line. It does not detract from the game for me. Traversing the city in the linear storyline and hitting the stops along the way, picking up some loot and perhaps eavesdropping on some unsuspecting soul to learn the location of a valuable, means I can complete the storyline when I want to and explore this open world as much as I desire...and what a gorgeous world at night it is! This game is beautiful, no doubt. It draws me as much as Skyrim (which I love to mod) and Assassin's Creed ever did. So, my only real gripe is the unnecessary X-rated brothel scene. It's the last time we'll likely see a Thief game, now that the immersive sim is going the way of the Adventure Game. But for fans like myself, it is a worthy final chapter for a game that defined a genre...as long as you don't have kids.

I love "stealth games."  The Splinter Cell  and Hitman series are probably my favorite francises.  I've played Thief: Deadly Shadows and thought it was okay.  This is the only other game in the Thief series I have played.

I did play this through to the end, which according to the achievements, only 15% of people finish the game. Why?
There's really no reason to play the game.
- The story is completely uninteresting.  I had zero curiosity about what would happen next.
- You steal items and get gold, but there's nothing interesting to do with the gold.  After you buy the few items needed to progress, there's really nothing interesting left to buy.  I finished with 6k in gold.  Stealling something usually gives about 10 gold.
-The vast majority of the game looks exactly the same: brown and dark.  There are only a few chapters where this isn't the case, and these were a lot more fun.  But I generally didn't enjoy exploring, because the world is not interesting.
- You can get "focus points" and level up, but only a few of the abilities are useful or interesting.  So you're not playing to level up, etc.

The only reasons to play Thief:
You are interested in finding and stealing every piece of loot in the game.  Each level tells you how much you found.
You are interested in completing various challenges offered (no kills, 10 knockouts, etc).

If you are excited about these challenges, I think you'll have enjoy Thief.  Some of the secret stashes are pretty cool, and I only found 1/2 of them.  The actual stealth mechanics aren't bad, and the various arrows (fire, water, blunt, etc) give you interesting options to complete stages.

If there were interesting things to buy, interesting abilities to acquire by leveling up, and if the world was interesting to explore, I would have enjoyed Thief a lot.

The Good:

+ A solid stealth game that actually allows you to play the entirety of it without confrontation
+ The grim-dark steampunk-esque world feels like it has plenty of depth and is ripe for subsequent titles
+ Replayability is there if the player enjoys the game and wants to try different play-styles


The Bad:

- Needed more polish in performance-related areas: cutscenes were laggy, lip synch issues, inexplicable lengthy loading times, etc
- AI could be unbelievably stupid or frustratingly hyperaware at random moments
- Game-world itself is confusing to navigate and tedious to explore
- The main story was confusing, poorly paced, and horribly delivered and characters lacked depth and felt like cardboard cut-outs
- Secondary missions in the form of "jobs" were a gigantic waste as a majority of your time spent completing them was traveling to the proper location


The Bottom Line:

Having never played the original series of Thief titles I can't make any comparisons or claims to how this 2014 revival stacks up. However, as a stealth-based game I can say that Thief accomplishes the feat of sticking to its guns by allowing the player to complete it entirely without open conflict or killing and that's something to be recognized as most recent titles in this genre tend to lean more towards action.

Unfortunately, the core gameplay mechanic is really the only thing Thief does well. Everything else here is just underdeveloped or unpolished. The story is weak and poorly put together, the characters are utterly bland, and the world itself in absolutely tedious and downright annoying to traverse. The games few cutscenes are jittering and laggy, the voice-work is dialed in and doesn't even synch up with the animations half the time, and loading sequences....even on a contemporary high-end rig, some loading times can be lengthy and/or the sheer amount of them can be bothersome (especially when moving through the map). 

It's no surprise that it's four years later and the Thief property has yet to see or even hint at any subsequent releases. Only halfway through it I wanted to stop playing and just be done with it and that only ever happens when I've been playing a game that requires 100+ hours to complete (Witcher 3, Assassins Creed Origins, etc). I powered through to the end though to finally finish a game I had started and stopped numerous since its release and I can honestly say you'd have to pay me a sizable amount to ever install this game again. 


Final Score:

The short version: This game is hot garbage.

Let’s start with the good:

(1) The stealth gameplay is decent.
There are a fair number of options for how you can approach missions, along with different tools and routes that allow for some variety in playstyle.

That’s it.

Now for the bad:

(1) The story is absolute trash.
And I mean SSJ-level bad. I honestly don’t know what the studio was thinking. It turns into this weird supernatural/virus/horror mashup… in a Thief game. Yeah. Bonkers. It doesn’t work at all. The characters are unrelatable and unlikeable, and the world itself feels flat and uninteresting. I could not be less invested in the story or anyone in it.

(2) The voice acting is terrible.
I didn’t realize Garrett’s longtime voice actor had been replaced, but it shows immediately. Everyone sounds completely checked out, like they just didn’t care. The writing certainly doesn’t help, but the performances make it even worse. It’s bad stacked on top of bad.

(3) The animations are rough and unfinished.
Lip-syncing is way off. Characters’ mouths move when there’s no dialogue and stop moving when there is. If you’re expecting immersion, don’t—you’ll be better off letting that expectation go early.

(4) Movement and interaction feel awkward.
Jumping is very limited, and there are constant loading interruptions mid-gameplay. For example, opening windows requires mashing the interact key multiple times or they just won’t open—and you’ll be doing this constantly. There are also tons of “walk through this narrow space to hide loading” moments, often combined with more button-mashing mechanics. It gets old fast.

(5) Tonally, the game has completely lost its identity.
It feels like a high school student who didn’t read the assignment and went off on a wild tangent about something totally unrelated. I was constantly thinking, “What the hell am I playing?”—and not in a good or intriguing way. You’ll be looting desks while monster screams echo in the background, paired with random horror “BONGS” that shake the screen or gray it out. It’s just… weird, and not in a way that benefits the game.

Overall, saying I’m disappointed would be an understatement. I cannot—and do not—recommend this to anyone, especially fans of the original series. I’m not having fun, and I’m not enjoying my time with it, which is surprising because this studio has made enjoyable titles in the past. Unfortunately, this isn’t one of them.
